title: Soft-deleted feeds can be reactivated through the wrong feed-type endpoint
reasoning: DELETE /youtube/{feed_id} soft-deletes the row but leaves the URL available for the shared create path. The shared create helper later looks up deleted feeds by URL only, not by URL plus feed_type, and reactivates the existing row without validating or changing existing.feed_type. After deleting a YouTube feed, a POST to /podcasts with the same URL and feed_type='podcast' can return/reactivate the old YouTube row even though the podcast endpoint validated a podcast request. The inverse can happen for deleted podcast feeds via /youtube. That violates the endpoint contract and can put feeds back into the wrong list/type after deletion.
reproduction: Create a YouTube feed with URL X, DELETE /youtube/{id}, then POST /podcasts with feed_type='podcast' and URL X. The helper reuses the deleted row matched only by URL and returns it with its original feed_type='youtube'.
recommendation: In _create_media_feed, make reactivation type-aware: either include MediaFeed.feed_type == feed_data.feed_type in the duplicate lookup, or explicitly reject a deleted existing row whose feed_type differs from feed_data.feed_type before reactivation. Add a regression test for both cross-type directions.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests were provided for the DELETE /youtube/{feed_id} feature, and no included test evidence asserts create-after-delete behavior across feed types.
suggestedRegressionTest: Add an API test that creates a YouTube feed, deletes it through DELETE /youtube/{feed_id}, then attempts to create a podcast feed with the same URL and asserts the response is either a 409 mismatch or a podcast-typed feed, never a reactivated YouTube feed. Mirror the test for podcast-to-YouTube if both endpoint families share the helper.
minimumFixScope: Update _create_media_feed's duplicate/reactivation branch and add focused API tests for cross-type reactivation after soft delete.
